title: A Multimodal Machine Learning Framework Integrating Genomic, Epidemiological, Environmental, and Clinical Imaging Data for Accelerated Measles Detection and Transmission Inference
abstract: arXiv:2610.32996v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Background: Measles resurged in the United States during 2025-2026, with more than 4,600 reported cases. Timely detection and transmission inference require integrated genomic, epidemiological, environmental, and clinical data. We developed a multimodal machine learning (ML) framework integrating genomic sequences, epidemiological indicators, wastewater surveillance, and clinical rash images. Methods: We evaluated a three-stage pipeline using public data. Stage 1 classified transmission linkage among 903 sequence pairs from the 2021 Ohio-Arizona-Washington outbreak using k-mer TF-IDF-SVD embeddings and pairwise single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) distances with leave-one-cluster-out cross-validation. Stage 2 predicted state-week outbreak risk using logistic regression and XGBoost with wastewater, mobility, and vaccination features under leave-one-year-out cross-validation. tldr: 该研究提出了一个整合基因组序列、流行病学指标、废水监测与临床皮疹图像的多模态机器学习框架，通过三阶段流水线实现麻疹的快速检测与传播推断。
en_tdlr: This study presents a multimodal machine learning framework integrating genomic sequences, epidemiological indicators, wastewater surveillance, and clinical rash images through a three-stage pipeline for accelerated measles detection and transmission inference.
